topics.title: Meaning and Definition of Consideration
explain: Consideration simply means quid pro quo, or 'something in return'.
It is a vital element; without it, a promise is not enforceable at law.
It involves a double aspect: benefit to promisor and detriment to promisee.
In English law, it is predominantly viewed in the sense of some detriment.
Under Section 2(d), it arises when at the desire of the promisor, the promisee or another person acts, abstains, or promises to do or abstain.

flow.title: How Consideration Arises Under Section 2(d)
steps: Promisor makes a request or desire
Promisee or third party acts or abstains
Act or abstinence forms the price
Valid consideration binds the promisor's promise

topics.example: Ajay promises to guarantee payment if Bhuvan sells goods on credit to Chaitanya; selling on credit is Bhuvan's consideration.
remember: Misa v. Currie: Consideration is a right, interest, profit or forbearance, detriment, loss suffered.
mistakes: Assuming consideration must always be money; doing an act or abstaining from doing something also counts.

quiz.why: Consideration is legally understood as quid pro quo, meaning 'something in return'.

quiz.q: Under Section 2(d), consideration must move at the desire of:
quiz.why: Section 2(d) expressly begins with 'When at the desire of the promisor'.

topics.title: Legal Rules Regarding Valid Consideration
explain: Consideration must move at the promisor's desire, not by voluntary acts or third-party request (Durga Prasad v. Baldeo).
It may move from the promisee or any third person; privity of consideration is not required in India (Chinnayya vs. Ramayya).
It can be executed (performed) or executory (a promise to perform in future).
It can be past, present, or future; past services rendered at previous request count as valid consideration.
It need not be adequate in financial terms, but must have some value in the eyes of law.
It must not be performance of an existing legal duty, nor illusory, illegal, immoral, or against public policy.

flow.title: Testing Validity of Consideration
steps: Requested by promisor?
Moved by promisee or third party?
Past, present, or future act?
Possesses some real legal value?
Lawful and not contrary to policy?
Consideration is legally valid

topics.example: An uncle successfully sued his niece for annuity because property given to her by her mother formed valid third-party consideration (Chinnayya vs. Ramayya).
remember: Explanation 2 to Section 25: Inadequacy of consideration does not void a contract where consent was freely given.
mistakes: Confusing voluntary acts with valid consideration; saving someone's goods from fire without their request gives no legal right to reward.

quiz.q: In Durga Prasad v. Baldeo, the promise to pay commission was void because:
o: The market was built without money
The market was built at the Collector's desire, not the defendant's
quiz.why: An act done at the desire of a third party (the Collector) does not constitute valid consideration for the promisor.

quiz.q: Which of the following statements about consideration is FALSE?
o: It may move from a third party
It must be adequate to market price
It can be past, present, or future
It must be real and not illusory
quiz.why: The law requires consideration to have some value, but it does not need to be financially adequate or of equal value.

topics.title: Doctrine of Privity of Contract and its Exceptions
explain: The general rule is that a stranger to a contract cannot sue, even if consideration moved from them.
In India, a stranger to consideration can sue, but a stranger to contract cannot sue.
Exceptions allow third parties to sue in trusts (beneficiary may enforce).
In family settlements reduced to writing, family members not party may enforce.
In marriage contracts or arrangements, a person benefited may sue.
Assignees of non-personal contracts and successors bound by covenants running with land can enforce rights.
A third party may sue if the promisor acknowledges or is estopped, or in contracts made through agents.

flow.title: Enforcing Rights Under Privity Exceptions
steps: Contract made between two primary parties
Provision or benefit created for outsider
Outsider falls under recognized legal exception
Beneficiary or outsider files suit directly

topics.example: Brothers X and Y agreed in writing on partition to pay their mother an allowance; she can sue them even though not a party to the contract.
remember: Stranger to consideration CAN sue in India, but stranger to contract CANNOT sue, subject to specific exceptions.
mistakes: Thinking a beneficiary of a trust cannot sue because they never signed the trust deed.

quiz.q: A stranger to a contract can sue in which of the following cases?
o: A cash sale between two friends
quiz.why: A beneficiary under a trust is an established exception to the doctrine of privity of contract.

quiz.q: What is the rule in India regarding strangers to consideration versus strangers to contract?
o: Both can freely sue in all situations
Neither can ever file a suit
Stranger to consideration can sue, stranger to contract generally cannot
Stranger to contract can sue, stranger to consideration cannot
quiz.why: Under Indian law, consideration may move from a third person, but privity of contract generally bars a stranger to contract from suing.

topics.title: Validity of an Agreement Without Consideration
explain: The fundamental rule is 'no consideration, no contract' (Section 25).
Exception 1: Written and registered agreement based on natural love and affection between near relatives [Section 25(1)].
Exception 2: Promise to compensate wholly or partly for past voluntary services rendered for the promisor [Section 25(2)].
Exception 3: A written, signed promise to pay a time-barred debt [Section 25(3)].
Exception 4: Creation of an agency requires no consideration (Section 185).
Exception 5 & 6: Completed gifts actually made and contracts of bailment (Section 148) need no consideration.
Exception 7: Enforceable charity contributions when the promisee incurs liabilities based on the promise (Kadarnath v. Gorie Mohammad).

flow.title: Checking if an Agreement Without Consideration is Valid
steps: Identify agreement lacking consideration
Check for Section 25(1) love and affection writing/registration
Check for Section 25(2) past voluntary service
Check for Section 25(3) signed time-barred debt promise
Check for agency, bailment, completed gift, or charity liability
Enforceable if any exception is fulfilled

topics.example: Mr. G promised Rs 1,00,000 for temple renovation; because the secretary incurred expenses relying on it, Mr. G is liable (Kadarnath v. Gorie Mohammad).
remember: Section 25(1) requires FOUR things: natural love/affection, near relationship, written form, and registration under law.
mistakes: Believing an oral promise between husband and wife without registration is enforceable under Section 25(1).

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT an exception to 'no consideration, no contract'?
o: Promise to pay a time-barred debt in writing
quiz.why: The exception covers past VOLUNTARY services under Section 25(2), not involuntary services.

quiz.q: A owes C Rs 60,000 barred by Limitation Act. A signs a written promise to pay Rs 50,000. How much can C enforce?
quiz.why: Under Section 25(3), a signed written promise to pay a time-barred debt is enforceable for the promised amount (Rs 50,000).
